edges.description: Occlusive coronary thrombosis abruptly interrupts perfusion of the downstream myocardium, producing ischemia.
Emergency restoration of coronary flow to salvage ischemic myocardium paradoxically inflicts additional reperfusion injury on the jeopardized tissue.
Massive cardiomyocyte death releases damage-associated molecular patterns that ignite the post-infarction inflammatory and reparative cascade.
Regional ischemic necrosis of myocardium is the infarct itself, so this node is what the clinical phenotype names.
Ischemic myocardium generates the prolonged substernal pressure or pain of the classic acute presentation, transmitted by cardiac sympathetic afferents.
The same ischemic afferent signalling also produces atypical and non-anginal chest discomfort, which is how a large fraction of infarcts present.
Ischemic and necrotic myocardium is electrically heterogeneous and provides the arrhythmogenic substrate for conduction block and re-entry.
Loss of contractile myocardium in the infarct territory reduces global left ventricular systolic performance.
Abrupt restoration of flow into ischemic myocardium produces calcium overload and marked dispersion of repolarization at the border zone, the substrate for reperfusion ventricular fibrillation.
Reperfusion-driven necrosis and DAMP release amplify the sterile inflammatory response in the infarcted myocardium.
Efferocytosis-driven release of TGF-beta and other reparative mediators activates fibroblasts and myofibroblasts, initiating fibrotic scar formation and structural remodeling.
Interstitial fibrosis and chamber dilation degrade contractile efficiency beyond the initial loss of infarcted muscle, lowering ejection fraction further in the months after the event.
Adverse post-infarction remodeling progresses to the congestive heart-failure syndrome once systolic dysfunction and neurohormonal activation raise filling pressures and cause fluid retention.
intermediate_mechanisms: progressive systolic dysfunction and chamber dilation
neurohormonal activation with sodium and water retention

edges.description: Ventricular ectopy arising on the ischemic substrate can degenerate into ventricular fibrillation, the malignant end of the post-infarction arrhythmia spectrum.
A sustained brady- or tachyarrhythmia drops cardiac output abruptly enough to cause transient cerebral hypoperfusion and loss of consciousness.
Impaired systolic emptying raises filling pressures and congests the pulmonary circulation, which is felt as breathlessness.
intermediate_mechanisms: raised left ventricular filling pressure and pulmonary venous congestion

edges.description: The oxygen gradient reproduces regional ischemic cardiomyocyte death and the arrhythmogenic calcium-handling defect, spatially separated within one construct rather than averaged over it.
edges.limitations: Death here is driven by diffusion-limited hypoxia in a construct with no vasculature and no coronary occlusion, so the model reproduces the consequence of interrupted perfusion but not its atherothrombotic cause. The cardiomyocytes are immature iPSC-derived cells.
edges.source: Human cardiac infarct organoid with an internal oxygen-diffusion gradient

edges.description: Myofibroblast conversion and tissue stiffening arise endogenously from the hypoxia gradient and adrenergic drive, without exogenous TGF-beta or a stiffened substrate.
edges.limitations: The organoid contains no leukocytes, so fibrosis develops without the inflammatory-to-reparative transition that drives it in vivo; the stiffening is that of acute remodeling and does not reach the values of a mature scar.
edges.source: Human cardiac infarct organoid with an internal oxygen-diffusion gradient

edges.description: Reproduces the electromechanical dysfunction of border-zone myocardium and attributes it specifically to the oxygen gradient.
edges.limitations: The chip models the oxygen gradient and its functional consequences, not the cardiomyocyte necrosis of the infarct core; there is no coronary circulation and no thrombotic trigger.

edges.description: Gradient-exposed cardiac tissue raises inflammatory-cascade expression on its own, showing that the myocardial arm of the post-infarction inflammatory response does not require leukocytes to be initiated.
edges.limitations: The construct contains no neutrophils, monocytes or macrophages, so it captures only the cardiac-tissue half of the response and cannot model recruitment, efferocytosis or the inflammatory-to-reparative transition that the node describes. The evidence is transcriptional.

edges.description: Reproduces reperfusion-associated cardiomyocyte death and contractile failure in an all-human system, and shows the injury is pharmacologically reversible.
edges.limitations: Oxygen and nutrient deprivation are applied to the tissue directly, so there is no microvascular obstruction, no circulating leukocytes and no platelet contribution to reperfusion injury.
edges.source: Human heart-on-a-chip ischemia-reperfusion assay with endothelial extracellular vesicle rescue

edges.description: Reproduces the acute electrophysiological response to oxygen deprivation, including action-potential shortening attributable to ATP-dependent potassium channel activation, but not the death arm of the node.
edges.limitations: HL-1 is an immortalized murine atrial line, so neither the species nor the chamber matches human ventricular myocardium, and the recorded action potentials should not be read as human values. The hypoxia is brief and reversible and no cardiomyocyte death is assayed, so the model addresses only the electrophysiological facet of this node.
edges.source: Bioelectronically instrumented heart-on-a-chip under acute hypoxia

edges.description: Reproduces reperfusion-associated cell death and functional loss, and isolates the epicardium's contribution by comparison with epicardium-free tissue.
edges.limitations: Injury is imposed on the construct without vasculature or circulating immune cells. The readout of interest is the difference between epicardium-bearing and epicardium-free tissue, so absolute injury magnitudes are not transferable to human infarction.
edges.source: Epicardial-myocardial heart-on-a-chip model of ischemia-reperfusion injury

edges.description: Identifies the epicardium as a source of the myofibroblast-like population that appears after reperfusion injury, by directly observing inward migration rather than inferring lineage from endpoint staining.
edges.limitations: Migration is observed over the days of chip culture and contributes to an alpha-smooth-muscle-actin-positive population; no collagen deposition or scar maturation is measured, so this covers the cellular origin of remodeling and not its matrix output.
edges.source: Epicardial-myocardial heart-on-a-chip model of ischemia-reperfusion injury

edges.description: Troponin reaches the circulation only when cardiomyocyte membrane integrity is lost, so a rise and fall above the 99th centile measures the cardiomyocyte-death step. CK-MB release also reports cardiomyocyte necrosis, with slower kinetics than troponin, which is why it was historically used to gauge infarct timing.

A microfluidic cardiac chip with integrated extracellular electrodes and intracellular platinum nanopillars, used to follow the electrophysiological response to a rapidly imposed and reversible oxygen deficit. Its interest is instrumental rather than biological: because the electrodes are multiplexed and read continuously, the transition from tachycardia through bradycardia to arrhythmia is captured as a time course rather than as endpoint samples. The cells are a murine atrial line, so the platform is more transferable than its biology.

nodes.description: Loss of contractile myocardium and sustained inflammatory/neurohormonal drive produce adverse structural remodeling of the ventricle. Cardiac fibroblasts differentiate into myofibroblasts that deposit a collagen-based extracellular matrix; a well-organized scar protects against rupture and limits acute dilation, but excessive, prolonged, or dysregulated fibrogenic signaling drives interstitial fibrosis, chamber dilation, and contractile dysfunction, progressing to heart failure. This node conforms to the conserved ventricular-remodeling step of the maladaptive-cardiomyopathy module, substituting the ischemic infarct scar as the disorder-specific insult.

nodes.description: Chest pain is the cardinal presenting symptom of MI. A coronary atherosclerotic plaque with a thin fibrous cap and a large necrotic core ruptures (or, less often, erodes), exposing highly thrombogenic necrotic-core material and subendothelial collagen to flowing blood. Platelet adhesion and activation with activation of the coagulation cascade form an occlusive or near-occlusive coronary thrombus that abruptly interrupts blood flow to the downstream myocardium. Systemic inflammation, including that accompanying acute respiratory infection, can destabilize vulnerable plaque and promote a procoagulant state.

nodes.description: A self-assembled multicellular human cardiac microtissue in which the infarct is produced by geometry rather than by a uniform treatment. At a radius of ~150 um and 10% ambient oxygen, oxygen consumption outruns diffusion toward the core, so a single organoid carries an apoptotic centre, a dysfunctional interior and a functional edge at once — the in vitro counterpart of the infarct, border and remote zones. Chronic norepinephrine supplies the neurohormonal arm. Because the pathology is spatially graded within one construct, edge and interior can be compared as internal controls, which uniform hypoxia (0.1% O2, which kills the whole construct) cannot do.

nodes.description: Human stem-cell-derived laminar cardiac tissues subjected to simulated ischemia and reperfusion on a chip, with a treatment arm in which vascular-endothelial extracellular vesicles are applied. The tissue itself is cardiomyocyte-only; the endothelial cells are the vesicle source and are not part of the construct. The rescue arm is what makes the model a test of the mechanism rather than a description of it: cell death and contractile loss are reversed dose-dependently by a defined intervention.

nodes.description: Restoration of coronary blood flow (by primary PCI or fibrinolysis) is essential to salvage ischemic myocardium but paradoxically inflicts additional damage — myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury (MIRI) — that can account for up to half of the final infarct size. Reperfusion drives a burst of reactive oxygen species, cytosolic and mitochondrial calcium overload, and sustained opening of the mitochondrial permeability transition pore (MPTP) with collapse of the mitochondrial membrane potential and cessation of ATP production, together with endothelial dysfunction, NLRP3 inflammasome activation, and multiple regulated cell-death programs (apoptosis, necroptosis, pyroptosis, ferroptosis) and dysregulated autophagy.

nodes.description: A microphysiological system that imposes a controlled oxygen gradient across engineered human cardiac tissue, isolating the border zone as an experimental variable in its own right. nodes.description: Massive cardiomyocyte death releases damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs/alarmins) that engage pattern-recognition receptors (TLRs, NLRs), driving cytokine (IL-1, TNF-alpha, IL-6) and chemokine (CCL2) production and recruitment of neutrophils and monocytes. Expansion and diversification of cardiac macrophages clears dead cells; efferocytosis then triggers anti-inflammatory mediators (IL-10, TGF-beta) that restrain inflammation and activate reparative fibroblasts and vascular cells. This tightly regulated inflammatory-to-reparative transition is essential for healing, but an excessive or unresolved response promotes adverse outcomes.
